newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan announces first government loans to Romania.
newsitem.headline: Japan announces first government loans to Romania.

text.p: Japan on Monday announced its first government-to-government loans ever to Romania, also the first such loans ever extended to a former East European communist nation.

A Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said the approximately 22 billion yen ($194 million) in loans was for infrastructure projects, with 12.8 billion yen ($113 million) for developing port facilities and 9.19 billion yen ($81.3 million) for building roads.
The loans were a coup for visiting Romanian President Emil Constantinescu's efforts to keep up the pace of his country's economic recovery.
The Japanese government's yen loans, normally tied to specific projects, charge only nominal interest but differ from Japan's grant aid in that they are expected to be repaid.
Buoyed by a visit to Bucharest last week from President Bill Clinton, Constantinescu on Monday gave an upbeat review of Romania's recovery to Japanese businessmen.
"Romania today can offer a broad array of advantages for foreign investment," Constantinescu said in a speech to business leaders on the first day of his three-day trip to Japan.
He said Romania was a prime example of an emerging market offering exciting returns for foreign investors.

Romania's reformist government, which took power last November after seven years of leftist rule, has been scrambling to meet reform targets and secure the confidence of Western lenders and investors.
Listing economic achievements since his government came to power, Constantinescu said inflation and unemployment were down dramatically while foreign exchange reserves were up nearly 35 percent.
"This (rise in foreign exchange reserves) was the most unexpected success because companies and individuals began to sell dollars for leis (the Romanian currency)," he said.
An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission visits Romania this week to assess progress in implementing reforms.
The IMF approved credits of $430 million for Romania in April after agreeing on reform targets. A first instalment of $86 million was made available immediately.
